title: zfs: unmount FreeBSD layers without MNT_FORCE
body:
MNT_FORCE was used as an approximation of Linux's MNT_DETACH, but on FreeBSD it revokes every open vnode on the mount. When one podman process releases a layer while another is still unpacking into it, the unpacking pull fails with "bad file descriptor" or "input/output error" from chtimes, open and write. A plain unmount returns EBUSY for a layer still in use and leaves the mount to its remaining user, which is the closest FreeBSD comes to a lazy unmount; the callers already log that as a warning.

done.  thanks.

> When one podman process releases a layer while another is still unpacking into it

The one calling `ApplyDiff` / `CreateLayer` should be holding an exclusive layer store lock. (There are those `LOCKING BUG` comments in `layers.go` but even in that situation the mounts should happen with a read lock, i.e. should not be possible concurrently with tar extraction.)
Hum, I can’t even identify the code that would say `… from ApplyLayer`.

Correction: I have to walk back "I reproduced his error". Checking my shell history & logs, my two loops only ever produced `layer not known` / `layer for blob ... not found` (the rmi/pull race). The only time I produced the chtimes error myself was with a hand `umount -f` on a layer mid-pull. So the EBADF report is Hayzam's alone, from Sylve running one `podman pull` process per image in parallel on 16-CURRENT/ZFS.

"from ApplyLayer" was sloppy quoting. The full message is `ApplyLayer stdout:  stderr: chtimes /usr/local/share/grafana/public/build/NewOrgPage.c43b7859fcaf9681e013.js: bad file descriptor exit status 1`, i.e. pkg/chrootarchive/diff_unix.go:115 wrapping the re-exec'd extraction's stderr.

I don't have a trigger to show. Fine to close this until one turns up, or narrow it to the MNT_FORCE vs MNT_DETACH semantics if you think that stands on its own.

edit: Since then: ran the same loops with a DTrace trace on two 16-CURRENT hosts (about 240 pulls, one disk-bound): no chtimes error, every forced unmount came from the pull process itself, and `rmi -f` blocked on the lock for the whole extraction, as you expected. Only the rmi/pull race showed up (`layer not known`, and `saving big data "manifest-..."` when the other process removed the image mid-commit).
